title: Peltola Denies Knowing of 'Spoiler Candidate' Scheme as DOJ Broadens Alaska Election Inquiry
snippet: Democratic Senate challenger Mary Peltola pushed back against allegations that her campaign planted a namesake candidate to confuse Alaska voters, even as federal prosecutors issue new grand jury subpoenas.
content:
JUNEAU, Alaska — Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola forcefully denied Thursday that she had any knowledge of an alleged strategy to put a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, pushing back as the Department of Justice escalates a criminal probe into potential election manipulation.

Addressing supporters at a campaign event in downtown Juneau, Peltola sought to clear her name amid growing political heat. “I knew nothing about any other candidate on the ballot except for me and the incumbent,” she said. “That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters.”

DOJ Broadens Investigation into Candidate Recruitment

The controversy surrounds Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher who entered the race against incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Federal investigators are now examining whether Democratic operatives orchestrated his candidacy to mislead voters and siphon support away from the incumbent Senator in a high-stakes race that could determine control of the U.S. Senate.

According to sources familiar with the inquiry, federal prosecutors recently issued grand jury subpoenas and document preservation demands following a report by The New York Times linking Peltola’s campaign to the recruitment effort. Additional subpoenas are expected as federal authorities determine whether criminal laws were violated.

Republicans Demand Prosecution While Peltola Decries 'Distraction'

Top Republicans have reacted forcefully to the developments. Donald Trump called for Peltola’s prosecution and suggested she should be removed from the ballot, while Vice President JD Vance characterized the campaign's alleged actions as a "disgraceful" attempt to steal the seat. Meanwhile, Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a Republican, ordered a state-level investigation into the matter.

Peltola, however, dismissed the accusations as a partisan hit job aimed at shifting attention away from key issues like inflation and rising living costs. “They can’t win on their record so they’re trying to intimidate me into backing down,” her campaign said in a statement.

Ballot Distinction Upheld by State High Court

Despite previous rulings by state election officials questioning the neutrality of the second Sullivan's filing, the Alaska Supreme Court ultimately ruled that Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. was eligible to run. To prevent voter confusion, election authorities confirmed that incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan will appear on the ballot clearly marked as a "registered Republican" and "incumbent," while his unaffiliated namesake will carry no party designation.
